'''Vladimir N. Kopylov''' (Russian: Владимир Николаевич Копылов) was a Russian [[physicist]].

Most of his career he worked in the [[Institute of Solid State Physics (Russia)|Institute of Solid State Physics]] in [[Chernogolovka]], near Moscow.

He received the highest honor for young scientists in the USSR, the [[Komsomol]] prize, for his discovery of thermomagnetic and galvanomagnetic waves, which can propagate in metals.<ref>{{cite journal
|author=Kopylov VN|title=A study of thermogalvanomagnetic wave-dispersion in bismuth|journal=Sov. J. Low Temp. Phys.|volume=7|issue=5|pages=611–622}}</ref>

== Education ==
Kopylov graduated from [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] in 1970, specialising in Radiophysics and Electronics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.dgap.mipt.ru/department/history/alumni/1970/ |title=DGAP class of 1970 |access-date=2009-08-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090716130030/http://www.dgap.mipt.ru/department/history/alumni/1970/ |archive-date=2009-07-16 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Career ==
Authoring many papers,<ref>{{Cite web|url = https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=sErTO-MAAAAJ&hl=en|title = Google Scholar|date = January 2013|access-date = February 8, 2014|website = Vladimir Kopylov papers}}{{Clarify|reason=ambiguous date format|date=August 2017}}</ref> his work in collaboration with I. F. Scgegolev and others led to understanding of the [[Meissner effect]] in high-T<sub>c</sub> superconductors through the surface barrier effect, also known as the [[Bean–Livingston barrier]].<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Kopylov VN, Koshelev AE, Schegolev IF, Togonidze TG|title=The role of surface effects in magnetization of high-T<sub>c</sub> superconductors|journal=Physica C|volume=170|issue=3–4|pages=291–297|year=1990|doi=10.1016/0921-4534(90)90326-A|bibcode=1990PhyC..170..291K }}</ref>
